punchline: Brown says perfectionism isn't a high standard, it's a twenty-ton shield carried to avoid shame.
thirty_sec: In The Gifts of Imperfection, Brené Brown calls perfectionism a twenty-ton shield. People carry it to protect themselves, but it stops them from taking flight. Its thought is that if I look perfect, I can avoid shame and judgment. Perfectionism asks what will people think, while healthy striving asks how can I improve. The difference is whose eyes the work is for.
